clue.text: Queen of puddings?

definitions.meaning: Queen ... was the wife of George III, a British queen consort
a dessert of fruit baked in a mould lined with bread or sponge, so it is one of the puddings

explanation.surface: A query about which dessert deserves the title of best pudding, nodding at the dish called queen of puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'queen of puddings' is a real dessert, which tempts you to treat it as one definition; it splits into a queen's name and a type of pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to George III's consort and to a moulded fruit dessert lined with sponge fingers or bread.

clue.text: Pound in money jar

indicators.note: in means this letter goes inside the next piece

parts.note: cash is money
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A pound coin sits in a money jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a container; here it is a verb, to clash.
explanation.definitionFit: To jar is to be discordant or conflict, as colours or sounds clash.

clue.text: Forever youthful wrinkly gal, see, heading for Scotch

indicators.note: wrinkly means creased, so the letters are rumpled into a new order
heading for means the first letter

explanation.surface: An old woman, despite her wrinkles, still seems young as she reaches for whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrinkly' rearranges GAL SEE into AGELES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageless describes someone who never seems to grow old.

clue.text: In general, it helps to be supple

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fitness tip: being flexible usually pays off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means bending easily and gracefully, flexible.

clue.text: Ultimately, subject raised stirred up passionate outbursts

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word that follows
stirred up means mixed, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Raising a subject provoked heated rants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred up' turns RAISED into IRADES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long angry speeches, impassioned verbal outbursts.

clue.text: Broken by premier of chefs, code of added ingredients proves a hindrance

indicators.note: broken by means split open by the next piece

parts.note: E-numbers are the codes for food additives in Europe

indicators.note: premier of means the first letter

explanation.surface: A chef's additives code gets in the way of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that encumbers burdens or impedes, getting in the way.

clue.text: Say, have you any idea who's the love goddess?

indicators.note: say tells you to speak the phrase that follows and listen to how it comes out

parts.note: a casual way of asking this is 'd'you know?'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you can name the goddess of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'd'you know' gives the goddess's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman queen of the gods presided over marriage and women, so she loosely counts as a goddess of love.

clue.text: Harrier bound to get black

parts.note: a bound is a leap or jump
jet is a deep black colour

explanation.surface: A bird of prey sets off to catch something dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrier' looks like a bird; it is the British Harrier jet, which takes off vertically.
explanation.definitionFit: The Harrier is a vertical take-off military aircraft, nicknamed after its upward leap.

clue.text: PM once great leader?

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister 1770-82
star as an adjective means outstanding, great

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister hailed as a great leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' with a question mark: Polaris has long guided travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris guides navigators northward, so it figuratively leads travellers.

clue.text: Mother better organised, chaps devoured by her

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother
tidier, more orderly; 'better organised' looks like an anagram signal but is a plain synonym

explanation.surface: Mum is tidier than anyone, and men fall at her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' tempts you to shuffle 'Mother better'; instead 'better organised' is simply a comparative synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who goes through men voraciously is described as a predator who consumes the chaps she meets.

clue.text: Time on river that captures special moments

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A lazy afternoon by the river is a time to treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The time piece comes after the river although the clue names it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic device records particular moments as pictures, so it is what captures them.

clue.text: Unfortunate windy sound on loo, girl may be heard?

indicators.note: may be heard says the word is said aloud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: what a girl does on the loo, she wees (urinates)

explanation.surface: An embarrassing noise in the toilet that a girl might be overheard making.
explanation.walkthrough: Some solvers read LOO + the answer as sounding like the name Louise; either way it is a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze is a whistling, breathy noise from the chest, an unwelcome airy sound.

clue.text: Haunt accommodating lucky character (retired), oh for the bottle!

indicators.note: accommodating means holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: a den is a favourite haunt or hideaway

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: Lucky Jim is Kingsley Amis's comic novel, its title character Jim Dixon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker exclaims over a large bottle found in a favourite hangout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucky' looks like plain description, but it points to Amis's novel Lucky Jim; 'retired' turns its hero's name backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A demijohn is a large bottle with a narrow neck, often wicker-covered, used for wine-making.

clue.text: Some steps taken, figured out puzzle

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance, a series of steps
saw, as in understood: 'I saw what he meant'

explanation.surface: After a few dance steps someone works out the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture cut into interlocking pieces to reassemble is a classic puzzle.

clue.text: Arctic hooker, she was scuppered by me, I said?

indicators.note: I said tells you to say the phrase aloud as a speaker would

parts.note: if I scuppered her, I sank her

explanation.surface: A sailor boasts of sinking a ship in polar waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I sank 'er' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This grapnel-like device grips ice to moor a vessel, so it hooks in polar waters.

clue.text: Rose that needs cutting, heavens mother inspired!

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so these letters go inside
needs cutting means it loses its final letter

parts.note: which and that are both relative pronouns
the sky is the heavens
MA is mother

explanation.surface: A gardener notes a rose that needs pruning and thanks heaven and mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that needs cutting' reads as pruning advice, but 'that' is the pronoun WHICH and 'needs cutting' drops its last letter before the heavens and mother go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid tea rose variety bears this name, after the whisky and ginger wine drink.

clue.text: Watch muscle gets into condition

indicators.note: gets into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a state is a condition
PEC is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: A gym-goer keeps an eye on a muscle as it gets into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To spectate is to look on at an event, to watch it.

clue.text: Matter involving educating appalling children, primarily?

definitions.text: Matter involving educating appalling children, primarily?

indicators.note: involving means containing the next letters

parts.note: a thing is a matter or item

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A wry description of a schoolteacher's job: dealing with awful kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the initials E, A and C, which go inside THING; the whole clue then describes the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruction of pupils is the profession, which the clue jokily pictures as coping with dreadful kids.

clue.text: With little manners, curled snakes on top of you

indicators.note: snakes as a verb means twists, so the letters wind into another order
on top of means the first letter, which sits on top in a down entry

explanation.surface: Snakes coiled up on you, not very politely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snakes' rearranges CURLED to CRUDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something crudely means doing it roughly or impolitely.

clue.text: Officer in triumph observing Scottish valley

indicators.note: in here means set within, so the officer stands inside the word for triumph

parts.note: glee is triumphant joy
NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A soldier triumphs while looking at a Highland glen.
explanation.definitionFit: This glen in the Highlands is famous for the 1692 massacre of the MacDonalds.

clue.text: Always playing music, supreme on the fiddle (missing you)

indicators.note: on the fiddle means crooked or cheating, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder, from which 'missing you' takes out U
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A musician plays supremely well on the violin, minus someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle SUPREME after taking out U ('missing you'). 'playing music' signals that the answer is a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian term on a score means the instruction holds throughout, that is, every time.

clue.text: Old curse, fifty squeezed into French accommodation?

indicators.note: squeezed into means put inside

parts.note: maison is French for house
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An ancient curse crams fifty people into a French lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a curse, the opposite of benison.

clue.text: Free deer trapped by heartless relation

indicators.note: trapped by means this piece sits inside the next
heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: an uncle is a relation
a buck is a male deer

explanation.surface: A deer is freed from a trap set by a cruel relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the centre C out of UNCLE, leaving UNLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbuckle a strap is to undo it, setting loose what it held.

clue.text: Metal chain, ounce perhaps?

definitions.note: an ounce is the snow leopard, an example of a big cat

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a metal
a line is a chain or row

explanation.surface: A metal chain weighed out by the ounce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ounce' looks like a weight; here it is the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard, also called an ounce, belongs to the cat family.

clue.text: Original character in lady encapsulated by bright talent

indicators.note: encapsulated by means enclosed inside the next piece

parts.note: fair weather is bright

indicators.note: original character means the first letter

explanation.surface: A lady with an original personality is wrapped up by a gifted friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural aptitude or knack for something.

clue.text: Some garden perhaps under final flicker of sun, which shines

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed after
final means the last letter

parts.note: an acre is a measure of land, which some gardens cover

explanation.surface: Part of a garden sits beneath the last glimmer of sunlight, glowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl gleams with iridescence inside shells.

clue.text: Cool Belgian briefly spoken?

indicators.note: spoken says the word is said aloud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a Fleming is a native of Flanders in Belgium; cut short, the word is Flem

explanation.surface: A laid-back person from Belgium chats for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortening FLEMING gives FLEM, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm means calmness and coolness under pressure, as in 'phlegmatic'.

clue.text: Something read thus in lecture

definitions.note: at university one reads a subject; this is one such subject, treated as a singular

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: a class is a lesson or lecture
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: Something is read out in exactly this way during a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read' is the university sense: one reads a subject for a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of Latin and Greek is a degree subject one 'reads' at British universities.

clue.text: Creative wake, say, to see off leader

indicators.note: to see off leader means its first letter goes

parts.note: a wake is a gathering after a funeral, an example of a party

explanation.surface: A creative type stays up at a funeral wake to see the chief off.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone with artistic, creative pretensions.

clue.text: In brief drop, royal character getting permission to fly

indicators.note: in means this piece goes inside the next
brief means shortened by its last letter

parts.note: to cancel something is to drop it
King Lear is Shakespeare's royal character

explanation.surface: A briefly dropped royal figure is given permission to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' removes the last letter from the word for drop, giving CANCE; 'In' puts Shakespeare's king inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Air traffic control gives a pilot clearance, an authorisation to take off or land.
